note: Simulated people only (agent/test/sim_users/personas.json); the gateway, its agents and the model are real. pass^k after tau-bench (arXiv 2406.12045); difficult people after Sim2Real (arXiv 2603.11245).

kinds.flipper: says yes to every game put to them, even on a day they turn out to be busy, then backs out by message once it is booked (70% of trials)
kinds.ghost: answers nothing (half the trials) or answers after the hold has lapsed (the other half)
kinds.budget: gives up without saying so after 1-2 questions or 3-5 messages from the agent in one go
kinds.drifter: stopped playing on one of their usual days this week, tells their agent once, then turns that day down
kinds.vague: answers in vague words instead of tapping a button (75% of questions)

armsNote: real/coop: 12 scenarios x 4 trials on Muse Glimmer; real8/coop and real8/hard: the first 8 of those scenarios x 4, the paired comparison (the hard arm was cut to 8 scenarios to keep model time near two hours); fake/*: the same seeds, 20 scenarios x 8 trials on the fake model (every member agent says yes to every listed time), the code-only slice. The student worker (:11447) was wired in but never called: in these talks every member answer came from code (acceptable sets, rules), so the model time is Glimmer reading requests and answering chat.
discarded: Hard-arm runs made before the flipper was changed to say yes on busy days (a flipper who only said yes when free never backed out, because a busy date is busy in every trial) were thrown away and the arm rerun; 4 real and 9 fake runs of the 16-scenario first plan beyond s12 (coop) are left out (incomplete k).

modelTime.note: summed time of the gateway calls to Glimmer, queueing included (the server is shared with the live site); two runs at a time
